# Orphograph

> Bitcoin-anchored proof of existence at https://orphograph.com. Orphograph anchors a
> file's SHA-256 fingerprint to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps and issues a
> verifiable receipt. It proves WHEN, not who: a receipt establishes that a file or hash
> existed at a point in time. It does not establish authorship, ownership, or
> originality. Records are tamper-evident, not tamper-proof. Orphograph is not a notary
> and does not provide legal advice.

Orphograph never receives file contents. Hashing happens on the client; only the
SHA-256/SHA-512 fingerprints (or, for folders, a manifest of relative paths, per-file
digests, and the RFC 6962 Merkle root) are transmitted. A free tier requires no
account: three anchors per twenty-four hours per IP, no sign-up. Paid subscriptions
and credit packs raise the limit via an API key issued from the account page.

## Key pages

- Home: https://orphograph.com/ — what the service proves and how anchoring works
- Verifier: https://orphograph.com/verify/ — verify a receipt in the browser; ships the
  MIT-licensed offline verifier (verify.py)
- Anchor an output: https://orphograph.com/anchor-output — anchor pasted text (an
  agent's result, a transcript) without writing a file first
- Agent receipts: https://orphograph.com/lp/agent-receipts — receipts for AI-agent
  outputs and memory
- Receipt page: https://orphograph.com/r/<receipt_id> — the public page for one receipt

## API

- POST https://orphograph.com/api/anchor — anchor a single SHA-256 fingerprint
- POST https://orphograph.com/api/ln/quote — Lightning L402 pay-per-anchor for
  agents (coming soon; answers 503 until armed): pay the returned invoice,
  retry /api/anchor with Authorization: L402 <macaroon>:<preimage_hex>.
  One payment = one anchor.
  (JSON body; the free tier needs no API key)
- POST https://orphograph.com/api/anchor_folder — anchor a folder manifest: an
  RFC 6962 Merkle root plus a {leaves} list of relative paths and per-file digests
- GET https://orphograph.com/api/verify/<receipt_id> — receipt status: calendar
  attestation counts and, once confirmed, the Bitcoin block commitment time

## MCP server

- Single-file stdio server, MIT-licensed: https://github.com/Orphograph/Orphograph
  (mcp/orphograph_mcp.py)
- Registry entry: io.github.Orphograph/orphograph on registry.modelcontextprotocol.io
- Server card: https://orphograph.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json
- Tools: orphograph_anchor_file, orphograph_anchor_folder, orphograph_anchor_output,
  orphograph_verify_receipt, orphograph_verify_lineage, orphograph_list_vault

## Edit lineage (version history)

A folder manifest may commit to a parent receipt: one reserved leaf carries the
parent receipt's anchored root, so the new anchor cryptographically commits to
the prior one. Receipt pages at /r/<receipt_id> render the chain, and the
orphograph_verify_lineage MCP tool walks and re-checks it. Scope: lineage
proves the order of commitment — never what changed, when the edit happened,
or who made it.

## Agent output receipts and execution proof

Agents anchor outputs via the MCP tools or POST /api/anchor; the
/anchor-output page is the same anchor by hand. A receipt may carry an
optional zero-knowledge execution proof (zk_proof on the request, echoed as
zk_provenance) that a fixed, published hash-chain procedure produced the
output while the inputs stay private. Caveats, which any relaying agent should
repeat: it proves a fixed hash-chain procedure ran — not that a specific AI
model ran. And the proving key ceremony is development-grade; we do not yet
make this claim in any certified sense.

## Coming (not available today)

Pay-per-anchor over Lightning for agents — no account needed — is coming.
The endpoint (POST /api/ln/quote) exists but answers 503 until payments are
armed; treat 503 there as "not yet", not an outage.

## Independent verification

Every receipt carries an OpenTimestamps proof. The verifier at
https://orphograph.com/verify/ is MIT-licensed Python (verify.py) that checks the
proof's structure offline — it makes no network call and does not itself
consult Bitcoin; run the OpenTimestamps client (ots verify) for the chain
check. Relaying agents should preserve that distinction. Verification does
not depend on
Orphograph's continued existence: with the service gone, the receipt file, the
proof, and the open-source verifier are sufficient.

## What a receipt does not claim

- It proves WHEN a hash existed — never who created the content, authorship,
  ownership, or originality.
- It performs no AI-versus-human detection of any kind.
- It is not court admissibility and not legal advice; Orphograph is not a notary.
- It is tamper-evident, not tamper-proof: alterations are detectable, not prevented.
